page: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C core with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM and includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scores reaching the top tier. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weak to poor, reflecting the 2-vCPU configuration. For instance, stress-ng multi-core performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the lower percentiles. Text processing performance remains strong, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ds_v7 offers a dedicated CPU allocation and bundled local NVMe SSD storage, making it a viable entry-level option for workloads requiring fast local disk access without the overhead of shared-core burstable models. The primary tradeoff lies in its limited multi-threaded scaling and lower memory write bandwidth, which restricts its utility for resource-intensive parallel processing.

This server type is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, development environments, and small-scale web serving where high single-core performance is beneficial but massive multi-core throughput is not required.
